subject: Food Science
title: Volatile Aroma Compounds
description: A 60-second lesson on Volatile Aroma Compounds.

hook.text: Coffee contains over 1,000 volatile aroma compounds. Your nose distinguishes them instantly.

buildup.text: Volatile compounds are molecules light enough to evaporate and reach your nose.

discovery.text: A strawberry's aroma comes from about 350 volatiles—but 15 key ones define 'strawberry.' Remove those and it tastes like sweet.

twist.text: Many fruits share the same volatiles in different ratios. Banana and pear use identical compounds.

climax.text: Cooking creates new volatiles through Maillard reactions and caramelization. Raw bread dough has few aromas; baking creates over.

punchline.text: Flavor is volatile chemistry. A strawberry is 350 molecules.

quiz.question: How many volatile aroma compounds does coffee contain?
options: Over 1,000—the most complex aroma in any food
